institutions: Tianjin Key Laboratory of Aquatic Science and Technology, School of Environmental and Municipal Engineering, Tianjin Chengjian University, Tianjin 300384, China

works.abstract: Seawater and brines contain substantial inventories of high-value ions, yet their extraction is constrained by dilute targets, concentrated competitors and feed-dependent speciation. Two-dimensional (2D) membranes offer short, tunable pathways that can amplify subtle differences in ion size, hydration, charge, and coordination. This review integrates ionic properties and aqueous speciation with membrane structure to establish a mechanistic framework for ion selectivity in 2D nanochannels. It critically examines size exclusion, dehydration, electrostatic partitioning, chemical recognition, and coupled non-ideal transport and evaluates their relevance to Li, U, Cs, Sr, Rb, and other underexplored ions. Major membrane platforms, including graphene-based materials, MXenes, transition-metal dichalcogenides, 2D metal–organic and covalent organic frameworks, layered inorganic materials and heterolamellar composites, are compared in terms of channel architecture, chemical tunability, stability, and manufacturability. The available evidence indicates that selectivity is not an intrinsic property of a nominal pore or material class, but an operating-state response of the coupled ion–solvent–membrane–electrolyte system. Finally, this review critically examines rational membrane-design strategies, outstanding challenges and future research priorities to guide the development of high-performance 2D membranes for the selective separation of high-value ions.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving a simultaneous enhancement of permeability and selectivity remains a central challenge in nanofiltration membrane design. Here, we report the fabrication of high‐performance polyether sulfone–cellulose acetate (PES/CA) mixed‐matrix membranes via phase inversion, employing polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as a pore‐forming agent and graphene oxide (GO) as a hydrophilic nanofiller to precisely tailor membrane structure and transport behavior. Systematic characterization using SEM, FTIR, and physicochemical analyses reveals that PVP induces the formation of interconnected finger‐like channels and macrovoids, whereas GO incorporation significantly enhances surface hydrophilicity and interfacial compatibility within the polymer matrix. An optimal GO loading of 1.5 wt.% enables uniform dispersion, maximizing wettability and transport efficiency; in contrast, higher loading (2 wt.%) leads to nanosheet agglomeration, reduced hydrophilicity, and restricted permeation pathways. The synergistic interplay between PVP‐induced porosity and GO‐enhanced surface functionality results in a finely tuned membrane architecture that alleviates the conventional permeability–selectivity trade‐off. The optimized membrane exhibits a stable pure water flux of 95 L m −2 h −1 , coupled with improved salt rejection efficiencies of 46% (NaCl), 75% (MgCl 2 ), and 59% (Na 2 SO 4 ), significantly outperforming pristine PES/CA membranes. These findings demonstrate a scalable and effective strategy for designing loose nanofiltration membranes, offering promising potential for energy‐efficient water softening and divalent salt removal from brackish water.

institutions: University of Jinan

works.abstract: Early permeability decline integrates both recoverable hydraulic effects and persistent membrane impairment, which limits its interpretation as a stand-alone fouling indicator. In this study, we evaluated whether pairing initial permeability loss (IPL) with post-exposure residual permeability loss could distinguish the magnitude and persistence of early hydraulic responses during ceramic nanofiltration. Six water matrices—drinking water, river water, reservoir water, secondary effluent, sodium alginate (SA), and sodium alginate supplemented with calcium (SA+Ca)—were examined using a 60 min early-response window, a defined deionized-water recovery procedure, and 8 h filtration trajectories. Apparent IPL ranged from 2.05% to 76.04%, whereas residual IPL ranged from 1.26% to 41.38%. Across the six matrix means, apparent and residual IPL were strongly associated (R2 = 0.948), while dissolved organic carbon was associated with apparent IPL (R2 = 0.871). Despite nearly identical measured organic carbon concentrations, the SA+Ca formulation showed apparent and residual losses that were 20.28 and 16.34 percentage points higher, respectively, than those of SA. Residual loss also increased progressively with exposure time, indicating that persistent impairment developed within the initial filtration period. Together, paired apparent and residual IPL provide an operational means of comparing early hydraulic-response magnitude and post-recovery persistence across water matrices under fixed membrane and operating conditions.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacially polymerized polyamide membranes have revolutionized industrial desalination, yet their intrinsically polar networks are poorly suited for molecular separations in nonpolar liquid hydrocarbons. Herein, classical polyamide chemistry is extended to hydrocarbon separations through the incorporation of a hydrophobic trifluoromethyl‐substituted diamine. Methanol was introduced as a cosolvent to overcome the limited aqueous solubility of the fluorinated monomer while regulating interfacial polymerization. Systematic investigation revealed how methanol‐mediated interfacial reaction kinetics and fluorination collectively govern polyamide network formation and membrane structure. The resulting fluorinated polyamide membrane exhibited a 12‐fold increase in toluene permeance and a 51‐fold enhancement in toluene/1,3,5‐triisopropylbenzene (TIPB) separation factor relative to conventional polyamide membranes. The membrane maintained 96%–98% TIPB rejection while sustaining a high average toluene permeance of 0.17 L m − 2 h − 1 bar − 1 during 21 days of continuous operation. Beyond model solute systems, the membrane demonstrated effective molecular discrimination in application‐relevant hydrocarbon mixtures, enabling the fractionation of representative Fischer–Tropsch liquids, rapid enrichment of linear α‐olefins, and efficient separation of light linear/branched alkanes as well as near‐boiling hydrocarbon mixtures. This work establishes fluorinated polyamide membranes as a versatile platform for nonpolar liquid hydrocarbon separations and expands the scope of the highly scalable interfacial polymerization technology beyond aqueous applications.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise hydrocarbon separations remain a major challenge for membrane technologies because molecular discrimination is often limited by poor control over pore accessibility and transport pathways in conventional mixed‐matrix membranes (MMMs). Here, we report a morphology‐engineering strategy that transforms the intrinsic pore anisotropy of ZIF nanoparticles into selectively exposed 4‐membered‐ring apertures within two‐dimensional (2D) nanosheets, which are subsequently assembled into highly oriented 2D ZIF MMMs. The pore system is reactivated through a soft chemical activation that removes residual surfactants while preserving structural integrity and solution processability. A shear‐flow‐induced pre‐alignment process directs the in‐plane orientation of 2D ZIF nanosheets within the polymer matrix, aligning the aperture channels parallel to the gas transport direction to maximize hydrocarbon molecular recognition. Multiscale characterization and simulations reveal a direct structure–transport relationship linking nanosheet orientation, aperture‐specific diffusion, and macroscopic separation behavior. The resulting 2D ZIF‐8 nanosheet MMMs exhibit enhanced mechanical robustness together with outstanding hydrocarbon separation performance, delivering a 332% increase in C 3 H 6 permeability and a 274% improvement in selectivity relative to the pure polymer membrane. This work provides a general strategy for programming pore accessibility and orientation in 2D MOF MMMs for precise molecular separations.

works.title: Demonstrating a Membrane-Based Process for the Recovery of Key Nutrients from Anaerobic Digestate Solutions
institutions: West Virginia University
works.abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates a two-staged membrane separation process for the selective recovery of two critical nutrientsNH4+ and K+from a nutrient-rich anaerobic digestate (AD) collected from a wastewater treatment plant. NH4+ and K+ are both critical for fertilizer synthesis, and their recovery from wastewater sources presents a sustainable route for nutrient production while simultaneously addressing the environmental issues associated with excessive nutrient loading (eutrophication) in local water streams. For this, a nutrient-rich real anaerobic digestate feed stock from a local municipal wastewater treatment plant was selected due to its high nutrient content: NH4+ (650−850 mg/L) and K+ (70−90 mg/L). The first separation stage focuses on separating nutrients from organic micropollutants using a surface-modified ionically crosslinked nanofiltration membrane. This stage produces a nutrient-rich (NH4+ and K+) permeate stream by achieving ≥80% NH4+ and K+ passage (1 − %rejection) and ∼95% organic pollutant (TOC) rejection. These membranes also effectively rejected multivalent cations, including Mg2+ (∼92%), Ca2+ (∼89%), and Fe (100%), and improved product quality. This membrane in the first stage also entirely retained the phosphorus (P) present in the AD in the retentate stream. For the second filtration stage, a synthetic solution containing NH4+, K+, and Na+ at concentrations representative of the Stage 1 permeate was used as the feed to evaluate selective NH4+/K+ separation. For this, a covalently crosslinked polyelectrolyte-modified membrane was used to demonstrate the partitioning of NH4+ and K+ in two separate streams. In summary, this study demonstrated the membrane-based nutrient recovery technologies for treating real AD matrices, extending their applicability beyond the synthetic matrices investigated in earlier studies.

works.title: Crown‐Ether‐Based Covalent Organic Network Membranes for Hydration‐Governed Li <sup>+</sup> /Mg <sup>2+</sup> Separation
institutions: School of Chemical Engineering Sichuan University Chengdu Sichuan China
National Key Laboratory of Advanced Polymer Materials Sichuan University Chengdu Sichuan China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective Li + /Mg 2+ separation remains a central challenge for sustainable lithium extraction because ion transport in confined aqueous environments is governed by coupled steric and hydration effects rather than ionic size alone. Here, we report a crown‐ether‐based covalent organic network membrane for hydration‐governed mono/divalent ion sieving. Unlike conventional crown‐ether materials that rely on cavity‐specific host‐guest recognition, the conformational flexibility and steric hindrance of dibenzo‐18‐crown‐6 induce locally ordered yet globally disordered packing, transforming the nominal ∼3 nm intrinsic cavity into sub‐nanometer transport channels with an effective aperture of ∼0.9 nm. Structural analyses reveal that the exposed ether oxygen atoms of crown‐ethers reconstruct oxygen‐rich confined hydration interfaces that regulate hydrated‐ion partitioning and migration. Thus, the membrane exhibits high mono/divalent ion discrimination, delivering a Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of ∼3900 together with high Li + flux, and also demonstrating efficient K + /Mg 2+ and Cs + /Sr 2+ separation with selectivities of ∼3140 and ∼840, respectively. Spectroscopic studies, density functional theory calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal a dual physical‐thermodynamic blockade mechanism, where steric confinement suppresses hydrated divalent ions and hydration‐mediated thermodynamic compensation facilitates monovalent ion transport. The membrane maintains robust performance under concentrated and Mg‐rich conditions, highlighting the potential of engineered transport architectures for lithium extraction and precise ionic separations.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Framework flexibility fundamentally limits molecular sieving in many metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) by enlarging their effective pore apertures beyond crystallographic constraints. This challenge is pronounced in zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8), where dynamic aperture expansion prevents CO 2 /N 2 size‐sieving despite an ideally positioned nominal aperture size. Here, we show that polymer infiltration enables in situ regulation of dynamic apertures, converting ZIF‐8 from a nonselective adsorbent into a CO 2 /N 2 molecular sieve. During mixed‐matrix membrane (MMM) formation, poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) partially infiltrates ZIF cavities and suppresses framework dynamics, as supported by solid‐state NMR ( 1 H‐ 13 C HetCor) and spin–lattice relaxation. Consequently, the CO 2 /N 2 diffusion selectivity of ZIF‐8‐NH 2 with 6 mol% 2‐aminobenzimidazole increased from 0.58 (polymer‐free) to 26.6 within the polymer environment, enabling CO 2 /N 2 size sieving. Membranes with 20 wt% filler achieved a CO 2 permeability of 261.7 Barrer and a CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 73.9. This strategy is generalizable to other flexible ZIFs, such as ZIF‐7 and ZIF‐67, establishing polymer infiltration as a simple and versatile route for controlling dynamic MOF apertures for effective gas separation.

works.title: Dynamic Hydrogen-Bonded Hydration Networks Mitigate Organic–Inorganic Fouling in Nanofiltration
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
Tianjin University
University of Science and Technology of China , , ,
Tianjin University , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Hydration layers are widely recognized as the molecular basis of antifouling membrane interfaces, yet their role is still largely viewed through a static barrier picture. The dynamic response of hydrated membrane–water interfaces to approaching foulants, particularly under organic–inorganic mixed fouling conditions, remains poorly understood. Here, using poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (pSBMA)-modified nanofiltration membranes as a model zwitterionic interface, we reveal that fouling reversibility is strongly influenced by the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks at the membrane–water interface. Molecular simulations combined with sum-frequency generation spectroscopy demonstrate that pSBMA sustains a strongly hydrogen-bonded interfacial water structure with preferential water dipole orientation under silicate and alginate perturbation, thereby suppressing long-lived foulant residence near the membrane surface. Real-time surface plasmon resonance measurements further confirm weakened irreversible foulant anchoring and enhanced interfacial reversibility. As a result, pSBMA-modified nanofiltration membranes reduced flux decline during mixed-foulant filtration to ∼6% and achieved &gt;91% flux recovery after physical cleaning, accompanied by lower organic and inorganic foulant residuals. Repeated filtration–cleaning tests with real secondary effluent further confirmed nearly complete flux recovery in complex water matrices. These findings revisit zwitterionic antifouling by shifting the focus from static surface hydration to the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding and regulating fouling reversibility.

works.abstract: Nanofiltration membranes based on the polyelectrolyte complex PSS/PDADMAC were formed via aqueous phase separation (APS) as a green fabrication route. The study examined structure – transport relationships in membranes formed from stoichiometric solutions of PSS/PDADMAC membrane on a polypropylene support. Two casting thicknesses, 200 μm and 400 μm, were used to investigate the effect of layer thickness on membrane formation. The morphology and surface properties of the membranes were studied by SEM, AFM, TGA, the electrokinetic method of measuring the ζ-potential, and the wetting angle of the membrane. The transport performance was characterized by ion-transport testing. The work focuses on how fabrication conditions affect the membrane structure, surface composition, hydrophilicity, and surface roughness, which in turn determine the separation properties of the membranes. This approach provides a sustainable method for preparing selective polyelectrolyte membranes and contributes to the development of next-generation water purification technologies that combine separation efficiency with environmental safety.

works.abstract: Abstract This research introduces environmentally friendly, sintering‐free, and cost‐effective hydrophobic geopolymer membranes developed through two distinct raw material routes, metakaolin (MK) and fly ash (FA), for water desalination via direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD). The MK, FA, and alkaline activator were used to prepare a geopolymer slurry. Hydrogen peroxide and egg albumin served as foaming agents and surfactants, respectively. Methyltrichlorosilane (MTCS), methyltriethoxysilane (MTES), and polymethylhydrosiloxane (PMHS) were compared as coating agents for the geopolymer membrane substrates. Results showed that MK‐MTCS exhibited the highest surface contact angle of 136.5 ± 1.8°. Additionally, the average pore size and vapour flux for MK‐MTCS were measured at 0.1339 μm and 11 ± 0.4 kg/m 2 ·h, respectively, and the membrane's salt rejection was calculated at 97.4 ± 0.7%. The study concluded that MTCS is an appropriate hydrophobic coating agent for geopolymer membranes used in DCMD‐based water desalination.

works.title: Reconsideration of Gel Polarization Model Based on Solubility-Based Flux Model for RO and UF Membrane Fouling
institutions: Alliance for Research on the Mediterranean and North Africa, University of Tsukuba, Ibaraki 305-8572, Japan
works.abstract: In reverse osmosis (RO) and ultrafiltration (UF) membrane filtration of soluble substances, concentration polarization can raise the solute concentration at the membrane surface above its saturated solubility, triggering precipitation until local equilibrium is reached. This surface precipitation reduces the permeate flux. We propose a solubility-based flux model demonstrating that, irrespective of whether the foulant is inorganic or organic, and regardless of the fouling pathway or the concentration profile within the fouling layer, the permeate flux converges to a constant value—the solubility-based critical flux—once the solute concentration at the fouling-layer surface reaches the saturated solubility. Application of the model to experimental data confirms its validity. Furthermore, the solubility-based flux model clarifies that the gelation concentration obtained from the classical gel polarization model corresponds physically to the saturated solubility of the solute in the bulk feed. This finding provides a practical guideline for membrane system design and optimal operation, including estimation of the maximum achievable water recovery.

works.title: CFD-Based Modeling and Experimental Evaluation of Fouling in Graphene Oxide-Modified Polyethersulfone Ultrafiltration Membranes
institutions: University of Shahrood
Islamic Azad University, Tehran
Islamic Azad University South Tehran Branch
Liverpool John Moores University
works.abstract: Membrane fouling remains a major limitation in ultrafiltration processes because it reduces permeate flux and increases hydraulic resistance during operation. In this study, polyethersulfone ultrafiltration membranes containing different graphene oxide loadings of 0, 1, 3, and 5 wt% were fabricated and evaluated experimentally. Water contact angle measurements were used to assess membrane surface wettability, while cross-flow filtration experiments were performed to determine permeate flux decline under fouling conditions. A three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics model was developed in COMSOL Multiphysics by coupling fluid flow, solute transport, and a resistance-in-series fouling formulation. The model was used to simulate temporal changes in permeate flux, pressure drop, and fouling resistance. Increasing graphene oxide loading from 0 to 3 wt% reduced the water contact angle from 78.5° to 58.0°, indicating improved membrane hydrophilicity. The membrane containing 3 wt% graphene oxide exhibited the highest initial flux and better flux retention compared with the unmodified and 5 wt% graphene oxide membranes. At 5 wt% loading, membrane performance declined, which was attributed to possible nanoparticle agglomeration and increased transport resistance. The simulated flux-decline trend was compared with the experimental observations and showed satisfactory agreement after model calibration. The simulated flux-decline trend was calibrated against one experimental flux dataset for the 3 wt% GO-PES membrane over a 30-min filtration period using a linear-regression-based adjustment of the simulated initial flux and overall trend. After calibration, the relative deviations between the simulated and experimental flux values remained below 5% over the investigated period. Graphene oxide-modified PES ultrafiltration membranes were experimentally evaluated. A 3 wt% GO loading reduced the water contact angle from 78.5° to 58.0°. The 3 wt% GO membrane showed improved flux retention under fouling conditions. CFD simulations captured temporal changes in flux and fouling-induced resistance.

institutions: California Institute of Technology

works.abstract: Abstract Weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels are emerging as a versatile platform for ion transport and separation, desalination, and energy applications. However, a predictive understanding of how dynamic charge regulation at the nanoscopic scale influences ionic mobility in these polymer networks remains elusive. Here, using large-scale molecular simulations, we dissect the coupled mechanisms governing small-ion transport in weak polyelectrolyte hydrogels, and reveal how charge density, competitive binding, and dynamic charge regulation jointly control ion mobility. By systematically isolating these effects, we uncover a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence of ion self-diffusion on hydrogel pKa and salt concentration for multivalent ions. Strikingly, allowing the hydrogel backbone to dynamically regulate its charge eliminates this nonmonotonicity and leads to dramatic enhancements in ion mobility, with diffusion coefficients increasing by more than a factor of 2 for trivalent ions. We attribute this effect to a protonation-assisted hopping mechanism that continuously remodels the local electrostatic landscape, providing an additional molecular-scale pathway for ion unbinding beyond translational escape and accelerating ion-pair kinetics without affecting the fraction of free ions. Our results demonstrate that dynamic nanoscale charge regulation can decouple ion mobility from equilibrium binding strength, offering a powerful design lever unavailable in fixed-charge materials. Building upon these insights, we propose simple molecular design principles for next-generation ion-conducting hydrogels and suggest alternative strategies for nanostructured membranes, energy materials, and biologically inspired charge-adaptive soft matter.

works.abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates the successful development of mixed matrix iongel membranes (MMIMs) incorporating high ionic liquid (IL) content and metal–organic framework (MOF) fillers to enhance CO2 separation performance. Three MOFs─Cu(BTC), MIL-53, and MOF-177─were incorporated into a UV-polymerized, solvent-free polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA-80) matrix. Dense and defect-free membranes were obtained and fully characterized in terms of morphology, chemical structure, hydrophilicity, mechanical properties, and thermal stability. The membranes exhibited thermal stability across a broad temperature range (298–473 K), although mechanical integrity decreased with MOF incorporation. Gas permeation experiments with pure gases (CO2, N2, CH4) revealed that MOF incorporation significantly enhanced CO2 transport, with Cu(BTC)-based MMIMs achieving the highest CO2 permeability (290 Barrer) and ideal selectivities (30.8 for CO2/N2 and 19.0 for CO2/CH4). Mixed-gas experiments under realistic flue-gas and biogas conditions (2 bar, 15–40 vol % CO2) further confirmed the superior performance of PEGDA-80 TFSI-10 Cu(BTC), including strong sensitivity to humidity: CO2 permeability increased from 216 to 412 Barrer at 11 vol % RH. The results demonstrate that combining high IL content with MOF fillers─particularly Cu(BTC)─is an effective strategy to produce thermally stable, defect-free iongel membranes with markedly improved CO2 separation performance.

works.title: Chitosan‐Gated Polycarbonate Nanochannels for Tunable Water and Cation Transport
institutions: University of Milan

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Biological membranes regulate transport by responding to pH changes and ion binding. Emulating this logic, chitosan is introduced into cylindrical nanochannels of multiporous polycarbonate ion‐track‐etched membranes via covalent immobilization or electrostatic adsorption. Chitosan is confined within the nanochannels, leaving outer‐surface liquid–solid interactions unchanged. The channels remain open when dry, while upon hydration the polymer swells and modulates water and ion transport. Chitosan shifts the membrane from microfiltration to ultrafiltration via swelling‐driven steric hindrance. Consistent with reduced water flux, the flux of tris(2,2′‐bipyridine)ruthenium(II) (Ru(bpy) 3 2 + ) decreases by ∼75% and ∼92% at pH 7.5 and pH 2.5, respectively, compared to pristine nanochannels. The stronger limitation at pH 2.5 arises from combined steric hindrance and electrostatic exclusion by protonated chitosan. Salts provide an independent stimulus: at neutral pH, they promote electrostatic screening, polymer‐chain reorganization, and chitosan deswelling, thereby increasing water flux, whereas under acidic conditions, the addition of KCl or CaCl 2 mainly affects cation transport through electrostatic screening, while chitosan remains highly swollen. This biomimetic platform enables pH‐ and ion‐triggered, bidirectional control of both water flux and cation transport under different pH and ionic conditions and thereby advances nanoporous materials for smart separations, selective ion handling, and adaptive flow regulation.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Gas‐produced water (GPW) is increasingly recognized as an important low‐quality aqueous lithium resource. Electrochemical lithium extraction using LiMn 2 O 4 (LMO) offers a promising strategy for lithium extraction from aqueous resources. However, its application to GPW is hindered by competing‐ion co‐intercalation and Mn dissolution, which compromise extraction selectivity and stability. Inspired by selective ion transport in biological ion pumps, a Li 0.33 La 0.56 TiO 3 (LLTO)‐engineered LMO interface is developed to integrate Li + ‐sieving nanochannels with interfacial stabilization. Experimental and mechanistic analyses demonstrate that the LLTO‐engineered interface promotes local Li + enrichment, while its Li + ‐sieving nanochannels restrict competing‐cation access, thereby accelerating selective Li + transport and optimizing Li + storage. Concurrently, the LLTO suppresses Mn dissolution, thereby preserving interfacial stability during repeated Li + extraction and release. Furthermore, the cyclic flow 3LLTO‐LMO//3LLTO‐λ‐MnO 2 system delivers 16.6 mg·g −1 lithium release capacity after 10 cycles and achieves an 87.5% Li + recovery rate while retaining 60.7% Li + purity from simulated GPW after 20 cycles, and further demonstrates applicability to real GPW. This work establishes a Li + ‐selective interfacial regulation strategy for efficient and stable lithium extraction and provides a material‐to‐process framework for sustainable lithium extraction from low‐quality aqueous lithium resources.

works.abstract: Abstract Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.

works.abstract: Abstract Separating surfactant-stabilized dual-type oil/water emulsions remains challenging due to the intrinsic limitations of traditional single-wettability filters. Herein, a heterogeneous composite particle-based bed was constructed by blending pristine hydrophilic MOF UiO-66-NH2 with oleyl phosphate-modified hydrophobic MOF UiO-66-NH2–OP. The mixed bed combines droplet capture with interfacial destabilization: tortuous interparticle channels promote hydrodynamic deformation, while adjacent domains of contrasting wettability are proposed to induce asymmetric interfacial stresses and Marangoni-driven film disruption. Subsequent droplet coalescence and interception enable separation of both emulsion types. Filtration tests proved the composite bed outperformed single-wettability counterparts for dual-type emulsions, achieving over 90% rejection and a peak permeance of 5861.3 L·m–2·h–1·bar–1. This work establishes an emulsion separation strategy via MOF wettability modulation and particle-bed construction, shedding light on the design of high-performance, tunable separation materials.

works.title: Pilot-Scale Assessment of Solar-Integrated Membrane Distillation for Seawater Desalination
institutions: Water Research Center, Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research, P.O. Box 24885, Safat 13109, Kuwait

works.abstract: Conventional seawater desalination technologies are energy-intensive, highlighting the need for alternative desalination processes that can utilize renewable energy resources. Although solar-driven membrane distillation (MD) is a promising approach, its long-term performance under Kuwait’s challenging climatic conditions requires further field evaluation. The main aim of this study was to design, construct, and evaluate the technical performance and provide a preliminary capital-cost assessment of a solar-driven MD system under Kuwait’s actual environmental conditions. The optimal operating parameters for the MD system were first identified using deionized water in an electrically heated operating mode. These optimized conditions were then applied to evaluate the MD system’s desalination performance using different saline water sources. The results showed that the water flux was higher with low-salinity feedwater than with the brine sample. Following the initial trials, the MD system was integrated with a solar thermal unit and evaluated during a one-year field trial under Kuwait’s climatic conditions. The system was scheduled to operate for six hours per day, although operation was occasionally interrupted by unfavorable weather conditions and operational limitations. The experimental results demonstrated that the system produced an average of 23.42 L of distilled water per day. These findings highlight the potential of solar-integrated air-gap membrane distillation (AGMD) for small-scale seawater desalination under Kuwait’s climatic conditions. Further investigations are required to assess its scalability, environmental benefits, and socioeconomic feasibility for practical deployment.

works.abstract: Abstract Selective Pt(IV)/Ir(IV) separation from spent proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzers remains challenging because of the similar coordination properties of their chloro‐complexes. Herein, ionic coordination microenvironments were engineered by combining the ionic liquid (IL) extraction systems to selectively extract Pt(IV) over Ir(IV) for the first time. The extraction system composed of 1‐aminopropyl‐3‐methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt ([APMIM][Tf 2 N]) and Cyanex 923 (C923) achieved a single‐stage Pt(IV) extraction efficiency of 93.1% and separation selectivity of Pt(IV)/Ir(IV) of 369. Spectroscopic analysis, quantum chemical calculations, and molecular dynamics simulations revealed the so‐called “synergistic ion‐association mechanism” resulting in the selectivity separation of Pt(IV)/Ir(IV). Stronger hydration stabilizes [IrCl 6 ] 2− in the aqueous phase, whereas [PtCl 6 ] 2− preferentially associates with protonated [APMIM][Tf 2 N] and C923 to form a stable IL‐2H + ‐Pt(IV)‐C923 complex, promoting Pt(IV) transfer into the organic phase. These findings elucidate the molecular origin of Pt(IV)/Ir(IV) separation selectivity and provide theoretical guidance for designing task‐specific IL‐based extractants for platinum‐group metal recovery.

institutions: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

works.abstract: Selective lithium recovery from multication aqueous streams requires translating the high selectivity of lithium-ion-sieve powders into macroscopic materials without compromising the accessibility of their ion-exchange sites. Here, hydrogen manganese oxide (HMO) was localized at the surface of a commercial polyethersulfone (PES) membrane through an adhesive polydopamine (PDA) interlayer, providing direct access to the active phase while preserving the porous membrane architecture. Microscopy and surface analyses confirmed the formation of an HMO-rich interfacial layer, and the resulting PES-PDA-HMO membrane exhibited a Langmuir maximum uptake of 35.6 ± 0.7 mg Li g-1 HMO, corresponding to approximately 91% of the experimentally measured capacity of the free HMO powder (39.1 ± 0.2 mg g-1). Under closed-loop recirculating flow, Li+ uptake approached equilibrium within 6 h and was accompanied by proton release, while X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy directly confirmed Li incorporation into the HMO-containing surface. Lithium removal remained similar across recirculation flow rates of 10-150 mL min-1 under the closed-loop configuration, whereas increasing the HMO surface loading from 5.8 to 8.7 mg cm-2 increased Li+ removal from 68 ± 2 to 99 ± 3% at an initial concentration of 50 ppm. After five adsorption-regeneration cycles using lactic acid at pH 2.1, the membrane retained 90 and 85% of its initial removal performance at 25 and 250 ppm Li+, respectively, with no detectable Mn release. Importantly, selectivity was preserved under severe multication competition: in a solution containing 50 ppm Li+ and 250 ppm each of Co2+, Ni2+, and Mn2+, Li+ removal remained 65 ± 3%, whereas removal of the competing divalent ions remained near 1%. These results demonstrate that interfacial localization of HMO can preserve its ion-exchange functionality after macroscopic immobilization while enabling selective, regenerable lithium capture under dynamic aqueous conditions.

institutions: Hunan University
works.abstract: Abstract Aqueous alkaline electrosynthesis enables production of formic acid (HCOOH) or formate (HCOO − ) using renewable electricity under mild conditions, but coexisting of alkaline electrolyte and organic product hinders downstream separation. Although membrane‐based desalination technologies are efficient, these processes suffer from product loss from transmembrane organic migration. Here, we propose that controlling the dissociation equilibrium of HCOOH/ HCOO − enables selective desalination of alkaline electrosynthetic formate by cation‐exchange membrane‐based Donnan dialysis. By simply controlling the feed pH, HCOOH/HCOO − exists exclusively as negatively charged HCOO − , exhibiting strong Donnan repulsion from the membrane surface and a high diffusion barrier within the membrane. Furthermore, using industrial waste acid as the receiver, combined with a monovalent‐cation‐selective membrane, improves the economic viability of formate desalination. This strategy converts the alkaline formate stream into a neutral solution compatible with established downstream processes, providing an energy‐efficient, scalable separation route for alkaline electrosynthesis.

institutions: Indian Institute of Technology Tirupati , , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Oil–water separation presents a global challenge, mainly attributed to the rising incidents of oil spills during large-scale oil transportation and the discharge of substantial quantities of organic pollutants by industries. In this research, Co3O4@ZnO-PDMS-coated nickel foam (NF) and copper foam (CF) composites were successfully synthesized utilizing hydrothermal assisted dip-coating method. In situ grown Co3O4@ZnO hierarchical structure on three-dimensional (3D) metallic foams was coated using PDMS polymer. XRD data confirmed the formation of Co3O4 and ZnO phases in the as-prepared metallic foams. Vibrational bands of metal–oxygen and silicone (Si–C/Si–O–Si)-based bonds confirm successful PDMS deposition. Surface morphology demonstrates 3D interconnected pores with in situ Co3O4@ZnO hierarchical structure and PDMS coating. XPS analysis confirms the surface chemical states and elemental composition of Co3O4@ZnO-PDMS-coated NF and CF. As-prepared metallic foams exhibited superhydrophobicity with excellent WCAs of 152° ± 1.5° and 152° ± 1.1° and CAHs of 4.2° ± 1.0° and 6.5° ± 2.6°. Superhydrophobic/superoleophilic properties enabled the as-prepared metallic foam to show effective oil–water separation with a good flux range of 4710 ± 223 L m–2 h–1 to 8469 ± 110 L m–2 h–1, high separation efficiency (&gt;97%), and reusability. The as-prepared metallic foam also enabled efficient gravity-driven surfactant-stabilized water-in-oil (W/O) emulsion separation with different surfactant concentrations, achieving a water rejection of up to 94.9%. The Cassie–Baxter wetting model interpreted the oil–water separation mechanism based on wettability measurements and intrusion pressure analysis. Co3O4@ZnO-PDMS-coated NF and CF composites retained hydrophobicity even after a thermal stability (50–200 °C) test and a strong acid–alkaline (pH 1–9) resistance test. Sandpaper abrasion cycle tests confirm its robustness, and by immersing in 3.5 wt % NaCl solution for 7 days, showed its anticorrosive properties.

works.title: A Heat-Resistant Polyimide Nanofibrous Moisture Diode for Thermal-Insulating Protective Interlayers
institutions: Donghua University
works.abstract: Thermal-protective textile interlayers must block external heat without trapping perspiration next to the skin. This requirement is difficult to meet because low-thermal-conductivity structures favor heat shielding, whereas wettable and open fibrous networks are needed for rapid moisture release. Here we show a heat-resistant polyimide nanofibrous moisture diode that couples thermal insulation with directional liquid transport. The membrane is built from a hydrophobic ytterbium oxide/polyimide nanofiber membrane (Yb2O3/PI NFM) heat-shielding layer and a hydrophilic lithium chloride /polyimide nanofiber membrane (LiCl/PI NFM) capillary layer. The low thermal conductivity of the Yb2O3/PI layer limits through-thickness heat transfer, while the hydrophilic LiCl/PI layer, with its bimodal nano/submicron fibrous morphology, draws and spreads water after it crosses the hydrophobic side. This asymmetric wettability and pore architecture rectifies liquid transport from the hydrophobic Yb2O3/PI side toward the hydrophilic LiCl/PI side. The PI(2:2) bilayer, prepared using equal precursor-solution volumes, shows a 54 °C temperature difference on a 200 °C hot stage, a water-vapor transmission rate of 7854 g m−2 d−1 and a one-way transport index of 957.43% from a moisture-management test, indicating preferential liquid transport from the hydrophobic side toward the hydrophilic side, with flame cessation observed after separation from the ignition flame during a qualitative flame-exposure test. These findings support further exploration of PI nanofibrous membranes for thermal and moisture management in protective textile interlayers.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) require stable high‐voltage cathode materials to meet escalating energy storage demands. LiNi 0.5 Mn 1.5 O 4 (LNMO) offers high energy density while employing earth‐abundant manganese but suffers from degradation due to manganese dissolution and electrolyte decomposition at elevated voltages. This work presents a facile water‐based process to coat LNMO particles with nanometer‐thin niobate nanosheets via electrostatically driven self‐assembly. As nanosheets of large aspect ratio (≈2000) are obtained by a spontaneous delamination yielding uniform thickness (1.8 nm), the coating consistently covers LNMO surfaces. Electrochemical testing in full‐cells showed improved cycle stability, enhanced rate capability, and reduced self‐discharge for coated LNMO compared to pristine material. Post‐cycling analyses revealed suppressed manganese migration to the anode, evidencing the coating's effectiveness as a Li‐ion‐conductive, chemically inert permselective membrane that mitigates detrimental side reactions. The modified LNMO/graphite full cells exhibit excellent cycling stability, retaining 91% of its initial capacity after 500 cycles at 1C, as compared to 42% for the pristine material. Additionally, the coated material shows an increased rate capability, with a capacity of 101 mAh g −1 at 5C as compared to 84 mAh g −1 of the uncoated. This scalable, cost‐effective, coating strategy extends cathode lifespan and offers a promising route for advancing high‐voltage LIB technology.

works.abstract: Abstract Replacing liquid electrolytes with solid ones is regarded as an essential strategy to mitigate safety concerns in lithium-ion batteries. However, the lower ionic conductivity of solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) compared to conventional liquid electrolytes still hinders their practical application. In this work, we propose a composite polymer electrolyte (CPE) by incorporating a poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) matrix with high-content lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) into an electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN)-based three-dimensional nanofiber framework. Active fillers of LLZTO nanoparticles and LiClO4 were further introduced into the PAN skeleton to construct additional ion-conducting pathways (designated as PLLP). This design of coembedding dual active fillers inside the electrospun nanofibers, rather than simply dispersing them in the PEO matrix, is distinct from conventional CPEs and provides continuous and fast-ion channels. The morphology and diameter distribution of electrospun fibers were optimized by varying PAN concentration. Consequently, the optimized PLLP composite electrolyte achieves a superior ionic conductivity of 1.12 × 10–4 S cm–1 at 30 °C, an electrochemical stability window up to 4.75 V, and a lithium-ion transference number of 0.53, which is substantially higher than those of conventional PEO-based electrolytes. Moreover, the LiFePO4/PLLP/Li solid-state battery delivers a high specific discharge capacity of 161 mAh g–1 at 60 °C at 0.5C after 95 cycles with a capacity retention of 96%, as well as excellent rate capability. These results demonstrate that the synergistic coupling of active fillers and a 3D electrospun framework provides an effective strategy for simultaneously enhancing ionic conductivity, electrochemical stability, and cycling performance in all-solid-state lithium batteries.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) are regarded as the promising next‑generation high energy density storage, but their commercialization is hindered by uncontrolled Li dendrite growth and the persistent risk of thermal runaway. Herein, a multifunctional artificial interface membrane is designed through electrospinning combined with in situ metal‐organic framework (MOF) growth, aiming to construct a highly safe lithium metal anode. The uniformly dispersed MOF nanoparticles in the membrane generate uniform Li + flux through their inherent cage window structure, effectively inhibiting excessive Li dendrite formation and thereby stabilizing the lithium metal anode with improved cycling stability. Notably, the membrane exhibits strong adsorption and catalytic ability for hazardous CO gases released during thermal runaway, enabling valid conversion of CO to CO 2 . Importantly, the ignition time of the as‐prepared Li metal composite anode is significantly prolonged, providing a valuable time window for battery fire accident response and personnel rescue. This work demonstrates a multifunctionally flame retardant interface protective layer design method through integrated interfacial and rational material structure engineering. It leads to a new strategy for synergistic suppression of Li dendrites and smoke toxicity in future safe LMBs.

works.abstract: Abstract MOF-303 is an aluminum-based metal−organic framework constructed from Al metal nodes and 1H-pyrazole-3,5-dicarboxylic acid (HPDC) ligands through coordination self-assembly. Its framework unfolds along the crystallographic “c” direction into one-dimensional rhombic/nearly square hydrophilic channels, with exposed bridging −OH and pyrazolic N−H polar sites on the channel walls, thereby exhibiting strong affinity toward water molecules and various polar small molecules along with a low desorption energy barrier. Leveraging its high specific surface area, exceptional thermal and chemical stability, inexpensive aluminum precursors, and environmentally benign aqueous-phase synthesis, MOF-303 has rapidly become a research hotspot in the international MOF community since its first report in 2018. However, a systematic review of its synthesis strategies and multi-field application advances is still lacking at present. This article comprehensively reviews the four main synthetic methods for MOF-303microwave-assisted, solvothermal, flask reflux, and vessel reflux approachesalong with their process characteristics and systematically summarizes the research progress of this material in atmospheric water harvesting, seawater desalination, heavy metal ion recovery, oil−water separation, harmful gas adsorption, biomedical drug delivery, and solar steam generation. Finally, this article deeply analyzes the common challenges and specific bottlenecks faced by MOF-303 across various application scenarios and outlines its future development directions from three dimensionsscalable production optimization, functional material modification, and long-term application validationaiming to provide systematic reference and insights for transitioning MOF-303 from laboratory research toward industrial implementation.

works.abstract: This study extends previous experimental investigations of a hybrid multi-stage solar desalination (MSD) system by developing and experimentally validating a detailed thermo-energetic model of the same installation. The system combines flat-plate thermal solar collectors with a photovoltaic (PV)-powered immersed electrical heater to supplement thermal energy during operation. A transient thermo-energetic model of the basin and eight distillation stages was developed, accounting for conduction, convection, radiation, and evaporation–condensation heat and mass transfer, and solved using the fourth-order Runge–Kutta (RK4) method in Python (version 3.12.11). The model was validated against experimental measurements collected over multiple campaigns and seasons using real brackish well water (TDS > 3 g/L) at Douar El Hamri, eastern Morocco. Quantitative validation yielded mean absolute temperature errors of 2.41 °C in thermal-only operation and 2.42 °C in hybrid operation, with corresponding mean relative errors of 7.10% and 5.00%, respectively. Daily freshwater production reached 45 kg in thermal-only operation and 93 kg in hybrid operation, while the corresponding simulated values were 44.47 and 92.84 kg. The hybrid configuration also reduced the Specific Energy Consumption from 689.15 to 387.20 kWh·m−3 and increased the overall energy efficiency from 61.83% to 63.12% and the exergy efficiency from 8.69% to 10.86%. These results demonstrate that the developed model accurately reproduces the thermal behavior and freshwater production of the experimental system and provides a useful basis for performance assessment, system sizing, and future optimization of hybrid solar desalination systems for water-stressed regions.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) systems face critical challenges associated with volatile organic compound (VOC) contamination in condensate and salt accumulation. Herein, a photothermal–photocatalytic BiOBr/MXene nanocomposite evaporator is engineered via crystal‐facet engineering and biphasic structural design to enable the directional conversion of toluene into nonvolatile products. The melamine sponge‐hydrogel substrate integrates MXene (97.25% solar absorption) with reactive BiOBr(1 1 0) facets, achieving an evaporation rate of 2.42 kg m −2 h −1 under 1 sun irradiation while driving stepwise toluene oxidation. Within 1 h, toluene is selectively converted to benzaldehyde, followed by oxidation to benzoic acid over 12 h. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that oxygen vacancies and Lewis acid sites on BiOBr(1 1 0) enhance toluene adsorption, whereas a built‐in electric field promotes photogenerated carrier separation, thereby facilitating radical‐chain reactions and suppressing VOC volatilization through conversion into high‐boiling‐point polar products. The biphasic structure further resists salt crystallization for 7 days in 14 wt.% brine through capillary‐swelling transport and dynamic salt regulation, concurrently enabling >99.999% heavy metal removal and phenol degradation efficiencies of up to 99.0%. This work proposes a “conversion‐over‐mineralization” strategy, synergizing high‐efficiency evaporation, salt resistance, and water safety for practical solar‐driven purification.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable freshwater production is one of the main issues for modern societies, and solar desalination is expected to play a significant role in the matter. Interfacial solar desalination is an emerging technology that demands highly efficient photothermal materials to absorb solar radiation and transport salty water from water reservoir to the hot surface, where sunlight absorption takes place, minimizing heat dissipation. In this study, a bicomponent solar‐driven interfacial evaporator made of Co 0.05 ‐Bi 2 S 3 /carbon foam (CF) (photothermal material) on a porous alumina substrate having vertically aligned microchannels was explored. The freeze‐casting technique allowed the preparation of a highly porous substrate (bulk porosity π b = 0.85) characterized by a low thermal conductivity ( k = (1.14 ± 0.06) W m −1 K −1 ). Moreover, the vertically aligned pores and the high fraction of open porosity ( π a = 97.7%) allowed for a fast water uptake along the sample (14 mm height in 5 s), making it a good candidate as a substrate for solar‐driven interfacial evaporation. The porous structure characterized by long vertical channels obtained through the freeze‐casting technique allowed for the preparation of thick samples without compromising the water transport capacity and ensuring a better heat confinement at the phase–change interface, leading to high performance. The best performing device showed an evaporation rate of (2.6 ± 0.2) kg m −2 h −1 , a value higher than most of the results found in the literature, making the sample a promising candidate for further studies thanks to the simplicity of preparation, the use of cheap materials, and the scalability of the applied technologies.

works.abstract: Abstract Freshwater scarcity is a major global challenge driven by population growth, industrialization, climate change, and declining freshwater resources. This review systematically and critically evaluates recent advances in nanofluid‐assisted solar still desalination, focusing on freshwater productivity, thermal performance, energy and exergy efficiency, stability, economic feasibility, and environmental sustainability. A systematic literature search was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 framework using Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar for peer‐reviewed studies published between 2022 and 2025. Of 343 records initially identified, 82 studies satisfied the predefined eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Unlike previous reviews focusing primarily on individual enhancement techniques, this review integrates metallic, metal oxide, carbon‐based, and hybrid nanofluids with phase change materials, advanced absorber modifications, AI/ML/CFD applications, techno‐economic considerations, and commercialization prospects within a unified framework. The reviewed evidence indicates that nanofluids enhance solar absorption, heat transfer, evaporation, and freshwater productivity, although performance strongly depends on nanoparticle type and concentration, dispersion stability, water depth, solar irradiance, climatic conditions, and still configuration. Al 2 O 3 and CuO exhibit strong thermal‐performance enhancement, whereas carbon‐based and hybrid nanofluids show promising photothermal characteristics. However, long‐term stability, environmental impacts, durability, cost, and commercialization remain major challenges. This review identifies current research gaps and provides future directions toward efficient, sustainable, and commercially viable solar desalination systems.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Competing heterogeneous and homogeneous nucleation severely restricts scalable, high‐yield synthesis of high‐quality covalent organic framework (COF) films, as bulk homogeneous nucleation generates particulate impurities and cuts film yield below 5% with exorbitant fabrication costs. Here we propose a screening‐effect‐mediated nucleation control strategy to fully suppress homogeneous nucleation by overlapping monomer depletion layers around substrate nuclei, implemented via a custom batch micro‐slit reactor that tunes inter‐substrate distance, polymerization kinetics, and surface wettability to achieve exclusive heterogeneous film growth. This approach affords high‐crystallinity COF films with ∼90% intrinsic yield and minimal particle contamination, applicable to 12 COF structures and capable of fabricating >1 m 2 films at drastically reduced costs (6.0–27.5 USD/m 2 ). The impurity‐free films display pronounced wavelength‐dependent photochromism from selective 350–500 nm absorption, enabling high‐resolution optical patterning for anti‐counterfeiting and sensing. This work provides a scalable, low‐cost route for COF membrane production and establishes a universal kinetic framework to decouple dual nucleation processes in 2D crystalline porous materials.

works.abstract: Abstract Graphene-based materials, including graphene oxide (GO), intrinsically lack stereocenters, limiting their usefulness in applications where chirality plays a crucial role. Covalent attachment of chiral molecules offers a promising strategy to introduce stereogenic elements into layers of GO. In this work, we report a one-pot method for the covalent functionalization of GO with lysine, exploiting the reactivity of the aminic groups of the amino acid toward epoxy groups located on the basal plane of the layers. Chirally functionalized layers of GO were prepared using d- and l-lysine and extensively purified to remove unreacted amino acid residuals. A comprehensive spectroscopic characterization confirms the successful functionalization, resulting in ∼3% N content. The chirality of the molecules bound to the resulting GO layers (relying on a rigorous purification by dialysis) was demonstrated through their interaction with a water-soluble porphyrin, which yielded chiral J-aggregates. The corresponding circular dichroism spectra confirmed that the porphyrin assemblies adopt distinct chiral configurations when templated by d- or l-GO. These findings highlight a straightforward route to impart chiral features to GO, expanding its applicability to several relevant fields, such as asymmetric catalysis, nanofiltration, and chiral sensing.

works.abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) are indispensable to technologies underpinning the energy transition, advanced manufacturing and digital infrastructure. However, their extraction and separation remain resource-intensive and are increasingly challenged by declining ore grades and the growing importance of dilute, chemically complex secondary resources. Biological processes offer a complementary strategy by exploiting molecular recognition mechanisms beyond conventional physicochemical separations. Biological macromolecules, cellular structures and metabolic processes create affinity-driven, three-dimensional binding environments that enable selective enrichment and recovery of REE groups, while high-resolution separation of individual lanthanides is currently achievable primarily through advanced affinity-based systems. This perspective examines emerging approaches to biological REE recovery, including bioleaching, biosorption, bioaccumulation, extracellular polymeric substances, lanthanide-binding proteins, and engineered biomaterials. We argue that their greatest near-term value lies in hybrid deployment, where biological systems act as selective solubilization, enrichment or polishing modules integrated with established hydrometallurgical operations. Particular emphasis is placed on scalable engineering solutions, including immobilized biosorbents and modular recovery systems compatible with existing metallurgical infrastructure. Realizing this potential requires a shift from proof-of-concept studies in simplified laboratory solutions toward validation in industrial leachates, rigorous assessment under realistic competitor-ion conditions, regeneration and reuse of biological materials, and integrated techno-economic and life-cycle analyses. Framing biology as a programmable platform for selective metal recognition and enrichment establishes a pathway toward hybrid recovery technologies supporting a more circular and sustainable critical mineral supply.

institutions: Northeastern University , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Metal-organic terephthalates composed of earth-abundant elements are promising low-cost and structurally tuneable anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their electrochemical behavior, particularly in newly developed compounds, remains insufficiently understood. We report monoclinic nanocrystalline ZnC8H4O4 (ZnTP-2), prepared through the controlled thermal transformation of a hydrated zinc terephthalate precursor, ZnC8H6O5 (ZnTP-1), containing residual terephthalic acid (ZnTP-1@TPA). This transformation involves TPA sublimation and framework dehydration, producing ZnTP-2 with fine crystals of approximately 50–150 nm, increased surface area, and a higher concentration of oxygen-related defect sites compared with ZnTP-1@TPA. ZnTP-2 delivers a reversible Na-ion storage capacity of 222.7 mAh g–1 after 80 cycles at 50 mA g–1, approaching its theoretical capacity and indicating highly efficient utilization of the terephthalate redox framework. It also retains 110 mAh g–1 after 500 cycles at 1000 mA g–1, with a relatively low charge-transfer resistance of 11.5 Ω, demonstrating improved electrochemical stability and rate performance compared with conventional metal-organic terephthalate anodes. Electrochemical kinetic analyses reveal Na-ion diffusion coefficients between 10–14 and 10–12 cm2 s–1, with the differences discussed in terms of apparent, Warburg-related and bulk/chemical diffusion processes. UV–vis analysis reveals a lower optical band gap for ZnTP-2 (2.74 eV) than for ZnTP-1@TPA (3.36 eV), with DFT calculations on idealized molecular models of hydrated and dehydrated zinc terephthalates supporting a similar trend. Full-cell examination provides proof of concept for its applicability.
